+=== Shlwid / Shwdeleg extensions
+
+The Shlwid extension adds the HS-mode read-write `hlwid` CSR, which
+sets the WID used for VS-mode and if not further delegated for VU-mode. The `hlwid`
+field is WARL that can contain Ceil(Log~2~NWorlds)-1:0 writable bits.
+
+If an unauthorized WID (per the `mwiddeleg` list) is written to `hlwid`, then
+the first attempt to fetch an instruction by VS-mode (or VU-mode if VS delegation
+is disabled) will take a precise exception indicating the software-check cause.
+Similarly, any attempt by HS-mode or U-mode to perform a hypervisor load or store
+"as VS/VU-mode" will be subject to the same `hwiddeleg` authorization check, meaning
+that it may also take a precise exception (indicating the software-check cause).
+
+When this exception is raised, the `mtval` register is set to "illegal world
+fault (code=4)". The software-check exception caused by Shlwid has higher
+priority than any access-fault exception (See <<exception-priority>> of 
+Privileged Specification) and leads to a trap being delivered to M-mode.
+
+.Shwdeleg/Shlwid extensions: Support for HS-mode to control the lower privilege mode's world.
+image::drawio/Shwdeleg_Shlwid.svg[Shwdeleg_Shlwid,align="center"]
+
+The Shwdeleg extension requires the Smwdeleg/Shlwid/Sswid extensions and allows
+HS-mode to delegate to VS-mode the ability to allocate WIDs to VU-mode.
+To allow for a hypervisor to set or context switch the VS-mode `slwid` CSR, 
+the `vslwid` replica CSR is defined as part of the Shwdeleg extension (see
+   <<hypervisor.adoc#_hypervisor_and_virtual_supervisor_csrs, VS CSRs in the Hypervisor
+   chapter>>).
+In HS-mode this register can be programmed to set the effective WID of VU mode.
+In VS-mode it takes over all functions of the `slwid` CSR.
+
+The Shwdeleg extension adds the `hwiddeleg` HS-mode read-write CSR. The
+`hwiddeleg` register represents a set of WIDs as a bit vector with
+WID _i_ represented by bit _i_ of the register.  The `hwiddeleg` CSR
+is a WARL register where each bit that can be set indicates a WID that
+is delegated to VS-mode. The set of worlds that can be delegated to
+VS-mode on a hart is platform-specific.
+
+NOTE: The `hwiddeleg` not only constraints `vslwid`, but as it is a virtualization
+replica that takes over the function of `slwid` when V=1, it also defines the
+authorized WIDs for the virtualized `slwid`. If an unauthorized WID is written
+to `slwid` in VS-mode, also then the first attempt to fetch an instruction by
+VU-mode will take a precise exception indicating the software-check cause.
+
+`hwiddeleg` is always a subset of `mwiddeleg`. Attempts to authorize a WID in
+`mwiddeleg` that is not authorized in `mwiddeleg` will fail - the
+WARL behavior will mask off any such bits. Similarly, if `mwiddeleg` is updated
+(either explicit or implicit), any WIDs that are de-authorized (set to zero)
+will be implicitly de-authorized in `hwiddeleg` also.
+
+If `hwiddeleg` is zero, the `vslwid` CSR is disabled, in which case
+any accesses to the `vslwid` CSR (direct from HS-mode, or indirect from the VS-mode
+`slwid` replica) raise an illegal instruction exception.
+Otherwise, if `hwiddeleg` is non-zero, the `vslwid` CSR is enabled. Like
+any other WARL register, HS-mode software is expected to read back the register
+to determine the actual configuration retained by the implementation.
+
+At reset, `hwiddeleg` is set to zero and hence `vslwid` is disabled.
